headline: A paper reports prompt-based manipulation of LLM serving length estimates, with fixed-output completion gains near parity
summary: The authors of JIL report a white-box attack that appends an optimized suffix to reduce the output-length estimate used by a TRAIL-style scheduler. In their end-to-end serving experiments, the system moved target requests earlier in queue order. The paper’s controls show that the headline 1.53× completion advantage combines scheduling and changes in generated output length: when output is fixed at 512 tokens, target completion speedup is 1.05 [0.92, 1.18] at 16 slots and 1.00 [0.97, 1.03] at 64; the fixed-output signal comparison against FCFS is 0.97 [0.95, 1.00] and 1.01 [0.99, 1.03]. The reported setup uses one model for serving, one GPU, and five small workloads; attack construction assumes white-box model/probe access and per-request optimization. These are paper-reported results, not an independent reproduction or evidence of deployed prevalence.
